intel_87210a61730c22b9.question: is AI data center growth driving US electricity demand increase?
intel_87210a61730c22b9.current_state: US electric power consumption per capita (World Bank EG.USE.ELEC.KH.PC) ranged 12393.4-13392.7 kWh/capita over 2010-2022 (no AI-specific attribution; series ends before the 2023+ AI data-center buildout). Separately, live-acquired evidence now connects: (1) global data centers consumed ~415 TWh in 2024 (1.5% of world electricity), growing ~12%/yr since 2017, with IEA naming AI as a primary but not sole driver (AI_ATTRIBUTION=PARTIAL); (2) IEA forecasts (not observations) of ~945 TWh by 2030 and ~1200 TWh by 2035; (3) a Jevons-paradox dynamic in general cloud computing (Google total energy +3.7x 2016-2022 despite near-optimal PUE), AI_ATTRIBUTION=INDIRECT; (4) ~130 GW stuck in PJM's interconnection queue with ~$3.5B estimated forgone savings, attributed jointly to data centers and electrification (AI_ATTRIBUTION=PARTIAL), framed as a generation/interconnection-queue shortage, not a transmission bottleneck. No source in this corpus gives a numeric AI-only (vs. general cloud/crypto) share of data center electricity demand. [v3 update] Real evidence has since been added for Europe (Ireland CSO: DC share of metered electricity 5%->22%, 2015->2024; EU EED Art.12 500kW+ reporting mandate, policy-only), the US (LBNL/DOE 2024 report: 176 TWh observed 2023 = 4.4% of US electricity, up from 58 TWh 2014, vs. 325-580 TWh by 2028 forecast -- kept as separate OBSERVED vs FORECAST claims), Korea (capital-region grid-connection bottleneck, 91.8% of contracted nationwide DC capacity concentrated in Seoul region per secondary reporting of National Assembly audit material, NOT independently verified against the primary document), and China (IEA ~100 TWh vs Goldman/Bloomberg ~200 TWh for 2024, both kept rather than resolved). Counterevidence acquisition also closed 2 of 3 remaining SEARCH_NOT_RUN directions with real findings (manufacturing/reshoring per Grid Strategies LLC; weather/peak-load per EIA/Ember, flagged as a peak-load-timescale finding distinct from annual TWh/yr demand growth); the DC-growth-without-power-problems region search ran but found no clear evidence either way (an honest negative, not a gap left unexamined). None of this new evidence provides a numeric AI-only share of data-center electricity demand in any geography. [O-1B update] Hypothesis evaluation layer audited and extended: H3 and H4 corrected from SUPPORTED to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED after applying a new deterministic Evidence Evaluation Contract (source tier / directness / AI-attribution-strength / temporal-type, plus same-origin independence checking) and 4 sufficiency guards; H1/H2/H7 reviewed and confirmed unchanged on quality grounds; H5/H6 reviewed, and a separate PRE-EXISTING discrepancy was found and disclosed (their canonical stored statuses, CONTESTED and WEAKENED, do not match what the unmodified classify_status() function would recompute from their own stored evidence arrays, which is REJECTED for both) -- left UNCHANGED as out of this phase's scope, not silently corrected. The H1/H3 relationship is now explicitly classified COMPLEMENTARY, not left as an implicit simultaneous-SUPPORTED artifact. [O-1C round-4 update] Hypothesis canonical write path re-evaluated: H1=SUPPORTED, H2=SUPPORTED, H3=SUPPORTED, H4=SUPPORTED, H5=WEAKENED, H6=WEAKENED, H7=SUPPORTED, each now carrying a canonical_status_diagnostics field (previous/legacy/quality-aware/final status, resolved/unresolved evidence, guard_trail) recorded in hypotheses.json. H1<->H3 both SUPPORTED is the expected, explicitly classified COMPLEMENTARY relationship (not a contradiction) per o1b_contradiction_resolution.json. New Geographic Applicability (o1c_geographic_applicability_result.json) and Temporal Applicability (o1c_temporal_applicability_result.json) sidecars were built this round, enforcing anti-overgeneralization rules (PJM != USA; US != Korea; Ireland != EU average; Korea contracted capacity != actual AI consumption) and OBSERVED-vs-FORECAST separation per claim. intel/hypothesis/hypothesis_model.py classify_status() is purely evidence-COUNT-based with zero quality/independence weighting (if supporting_evidence and not contradicting_evidence: return SUPPORTED). As of this update it marks H1 (hyp_b0a4bbbc9b601728, 'AI data centers are a significant driver of electricity demand growth') and H3 (hyp_o0_h3_ai_energy_infra, 'recent demand growth results from multiple non-AI factors') BOTH as SUPPORTED simultaneously, even though they represent competing explanations -- because each merely has >=1 supporting claim and 0 directly-contradicting claims in the model's narrow count-based sense. This is a disclosed structural limitation of the current hypothesis model, not a data error and not silently corrected here: classify_status() was intentionally left unmodified this phase per explicit instruction, since rewriting its logic would be an unscoped architecture change. Any report or synthesis reading H1/H3 status must present both as SUPPORTED-under-this-model while explicitly flagging that the model cannot currently adjudicate between competing hypotheses by evidence quality, independence, or directness of contradiction. [O-1B update] PARTIALLY RESOLVED: a new, additive Evidence Evaluation Contract (intel/hypothesis/evidence_evaluation.py) and deterministic sufficiency guards (Forecast/AI-Attribution/Derivative-Evidence/Industry-Self-Report) were added in intel/hypothesis/hypothesis_model.py.evaluate_hypothesis_sufficiency(), and applied to the real AI_ENERGY_INFRA corpus. Result: H3 (hyp_o0_h3_ai_energy_infra) is downgraded from SUPPORTED to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED (its 4 supporting_evidence references do not resolve to any evaluable Claim record -- SOURCE_TIER/DIRECTNESS both UNKNOWN across the board), and H4 is likewise downgraded to PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED for the same reason. H1 remains SUPPORTED on its own evidentiary merits (passes every guard, with real PRIMARY_RESEARCH-tier, AI_PARTIAL-attribution evidence). The H1/H3 relationship is now explicitly classified as COMPLEMENTARY (not MUTUALLY_EXCLUSIVE) in intel/hypothesis/o1b_contradiction_resolution.json, with full reasoning. NOT fully resolved: classify_status() itself (the plain count-based function) is left unmodified and is still what upsert_hypothesis() uses on every future evidence append -- a hypothesis corrected by this new layer will silently revert to its count-based status on its next evidence-array update unless evaluate_hypothesis_sufficiency() is re-applied. That residual architectural gap is why this is PARTIALLY_RESOLVED, not RESOLVED. [O-1C round-4 update] Re-evaluated against Te's section 24 six conditions: (1) canonical write path quality-aware = YES (evaluate_hypothesis_sufficiency() is the live write path for this round's H1-H7 re-evaluation); (2) unresolved-evidence guard working = YES (verified operating during the round-2/3 canonical migration); (3) migrated evidence canonical resolution complete = PARTIALLY (most key GridLab/manufacturing-reshoring/EV/climate evidence migrated to canonical Claims claim_a11c5cb4c7c4c2d1/claim_f5842e6162c8fefc/claim_d641fb1790c3ef53, but a few references -- e.g. the IEA executive-summary citation and the Ireland CSO reference underlying H4 -- remain pointed at non-Claim provenance strings rather than resolvable Claim records, and population-growth/industrial-policy alternatives remain under-researched); (4) geography applicability reflected = YES (o1c_geographic_applicability_result.json, new this round); (5) temporal applicability reflected = YES (o1c_temporal_applicability_result.json, new this round); (6) status-reversion test passing = YES. Because condition (3) is only PARTIALLY satisfied, this gap stays PARTIALLY_RESOLVED rather than RESOLVED -- classify_status() itself is also still unmodified, which remains the deeper residual architectural gap.

Confirmed again this round across all 14 canonical claims and all 7 geographic-applicability regions: no source (IEA, LBNL/DOE, Ireland CSO, Carbon Brief/Oxford on China, Korea National Assembly secondary reporting) gives a numeric AI-only (vs general cloud/crypto/colocation) TWh or percentage split of data-center electricity demand, in any geography. This is distinct from the pre-existing ATTRIBUTION_GAP (which concerns the older World Bank per-capita series) and is recorded separately because it now rests on explicit cross-referencing of the full claims/hypothesis/geographic/temporal/alternative-explanations evidence base rather than a single series.
